The next flush must resolve that exact key (via `resolveByExactGet`) before it may allocate a new transaction id, which is what realizes INV-14 (fail-closed on ambiguity) and prevents the ledger from ever silently creating a gap or double-publishing.

topic: RefTableState holds a copy-on-write map of committed rows
canonical_claim: `RefTableState` holds a copy-on-write map of committed rows, a set of precommits, an O(1) manifest-ownership index enforcing the one-owner-per-manifest invariant, a lifecycle (`Live`/`Removed`), the greatest applied transaction id, and O(1)-maintained body-size counters for admission. Two mutexes have a fixed lock order `ref_queue_mutex -> state_mutex`, never the reverse, and network I/O is never performed under `state_mutex`, so a reader sees either a whole transaction or none of it.

topic: Recovery of a ref table on first touch
canonical_claim: Recovery of a ref table on first touch performs a paginated LIST of `cas/ns/stream/<life-id>/`, takes the greatest snapshot, replays every log strictly greater than it one transaction at a time, restarts on a vanished object (bounded at 3 attempts, treated as concurrent GC cleanup rather than corruption), and on an unclean boundary publishes a recovery seal snapshot at the synthetic id `{my_epoch - 1, UINT64_MAX}` before exposing the table, so that id dominates any straggler the dead epoch could still materialize.

topic: Under CAS's RefLaneState model, relink certification is Ready-state-only
canonical_claim: Under CAS's `RefLaneState` model, relink certification is Ready-state-only: a resumed relink gate consumes a single-state precondition instead of the twelve-row cross-product the earlier encoding required, and the NETWORK_ERROR/terminal split means only `Closed`/`Faulted` are non-retriable while all other states retry.

topic: The ref state machine's load-bearing invariant is that
canonical_claim: The ref state machine's load-bearing invariant is that `promote` never silently displaces a different committed row for the same name; a silent displacement would never emit the evicted manifest's -1 edge, leaking it phantom-alive forever. `stateFromSnapshot` round-trips a hand-built snapshot through the codec so the same bug class cannot enter via snapshot loading.

topic: cleanupRefObjects only deletes ref logs/snapshots that are covered
canonical_claim: `cleanupRefObjects` only deletes ref logs/snapshots that are covered by BOTH the durable fold cursor AND a durable snapshot; GC never invents a ref transition, and dead-precommit cleanup (appending exact owner_transition removals) is the writer's job, not GC's.

topic: Ref transaction IDs (RefTxnId = {writer_epoch, ref_sequence}) are
canonical_claim: Ref transaction IDs (`RefTxnId = {writer_epoch, ref_sequence}`) are strictly increasing with epoch as the primary component, so a recreated namespace always gets greater ids than a prior life — no ABA check is needed on ref-log ordering.

topic: Loose mountpoint files are not namespaces — they
canonical_claim: Loose mountpoint files are not namespaces — they are path-owned plain objects with conditional overwrite/exact deletion, drained by server-root decommission. Directory creation has no durable representation and creates no catalog row. Detached and moving parts are ref-name prefixes inside the owning table's namespace, not separate namespaces.

topic: CA namespace mapping: a detached part uses the
canonical_claim: CA namespace mapping: a detached part uses the same table namespace with ref `detached/<part>` (no parallel namespace, B181 fold); a FREEZE shadow uses the literal shadow table directory as namespace (bijective, pool-global); verbatim table-level files (`format_version.txt`, `deduplication_logs/…`, mutation entries) are namespace files; loose startup-probe files are plain mountpoint objects at `roots/<server_root_id>/<path>`.

topic: Mutable per-part files (kMutablePerPartFiles: uuid.txt, txn_version.txt, metadata_version.
canonical_claim: Mutable per-part files (`kMutablePerPartFiles`: `uuid.txt`, `txn_version.txt`, `metadata_version.txt`, plus `.tmp` siblings) live in `RefPayload.mutable_files`, never in the shared manifest tree, and are matched on the last path component only.

topic: CasManifestCodec (CAPT magic) encodes format_version, writer_version, ref{epoch,seq,ordina
canonical_claim: `CasManifestCodec` (`CAPT` magic) encodes `format_version`, `writer_version`, `ref{epoch,seq,ordinal}`, the namespace, a `payload_digest` (integrity/debug only, never a key/dedup/in-degree input), and entries as an embedded RunFile keyed by path; the decoder enforces strict ascending canonical path order and rejects duplicate paths, an invariant `findEntry`/`entryRange` binary search relies on.

topic: Projection files are nested keys in the parent
canonical_claim: Projection files are nested keys in the parent part's single manifest at paths such as <proj>.proj/<file>, rather than separate refs or sub-manifests.

canonical_claim: The mutable per-(namespace, shard) root-shard manifest was removed by `318291fe5e5` and replaced with `CasRefSnapshotCodec`, `CasRefLogCodec`, and `CasRefIntake`.

topic: Store::mutateShard groups mutations for one (namespace, shard) into

topic: A CAS snapshot copies the table's current _snap

topic: A byte-equal repoint performs zero pool mutations, including
canonical_claim: A byte-equal repoint performs zero pool mutations, including no manifest PUT and no ref-log record.

topic: For trimmed-but-live precommits whose create event was trimmed

topic: The observability package emits ManifestPut after Build::stageManifest writes
canonical_claim: The observability package emits `ManifestPut` after `Build::stageManifest` writes a body and emits `PrecommitRemoved` after `Build::abandon` removes a precommit binding.

topic: readManifest remains a by-value compatibility shim over readManifestShared

topic: adoptPartFromManifest is consolidated onto publishEntries; sender identity is
canonical_claim: `adoptPartFromManifest` is consolidated onto `publishEntries`; sender identity is non-authoritative, while decoded entries are adopted as tokenless write evidence and re-proved during promotion.

topic: shard_decode_cache remains in Cas::Store with its TTL, shard_write_seq
canonical_claim: `shard_decode_cache` remains in `Cas::Store` with its TTL, `shard_write_seq`, and single-flight machinery, and `dedup_cache` remains there because neither should move into a new aggregate cache state.

topic: republishRef is idempotent when the destination is already
canonical_claim: republishRef is idempotent when the destination is already committed with the same content; a different-content destination is an ABORTED conflict.

topic: In the obsolete ref-log design, cas/refs is only
canonical_claim: In the obsolete ref-log design, `cas/refs` is only an append-only inbox from the mounted writer to GC, and authoritative namespace state is the adopted GC ref fold plus the contiguous writer-log tail.

topic: Phase 1 of the obsolete ref-log design rewrites
canonical_claim: Phase 1 of the obsolete ref-log design rewrites one complete folded ref base for each productive handoff, while idle and deferred rounds carry the exact parent base without reading or rewriting it.

topic: A table's durable ref state is latest table
canonical_claim: A table's durable ref state is `latest table snapshot + table transaction logs after that snapshot`; snapshots are complete table states and each log object is one atomic writer transaction.

topic: Live snapshots are published only by the writer
canonical_claim: Live snapshots are published only by the writer from its complete cached state; GC never reconstructs table state and may publish only the constant-size `Removed` snapshot for a removed namespace.

topic: Phase 1 replaces mutable RootShardManifest ref storage with
canonical_claim: Phase 1 replaces mutable `RootShardManifest` ref storage with an immutable snapshot+log protocol.

topic: The wiring tests stop accepting legacy numeric ref-shard
canonical_claim: The wiring tests stop accepting legacy numeric ref-shard keys and classify current ref writes under `/cas/refs/` with `_log/` or `_snap/`; the two disabled tree-model tests remain deliberate documentation.

topic: The recovery seal is the only snapshot whose
canonical_claim: The recovery seal is the only snapshot whose ID is an upper bound of a covered region rather than a real transaction ID.

canonical_claim: `snapshot_min_log_age_ms`, its age gates, `CasRefLatePredecessorObserved`, and young-entry replay bookkeeping are removed from the ref protocol.

topic: Committed-part standalone add and overwrite operations use an
canonical_claim: Committed-part standalone add and overwrite operations use an audited manifest repoint rather than failing closed or silently doing nothing.

topic: The writer's snapshot publication policy gains an age
canonical_claim: The writer's snapshot publication policy gains an age trigger so slowly changing tables periodically publish a small snapshot and do not leave readers with an ancient base.

topic: The ref-table-copy performance investigation identified three candidate mechanisms
canonical_claim: The ref-table-copy performance investigation identified three candidate mechanisms for reducing `flushRefBatch` copying from whole-map cost to touched-row cost: a persistent immutable map, an overlay/delta over a shared base, and a copy-on-write wrapper over `std::map`.

topic: The corrected identity design publishes a cloned part
canonical_claim: The corrected identity design publishes a cloned part under transient ref `moving/<part>` and makes `rename(moving/<part> → <part>)` a committed-ref repoint onto the final ref.

canonical_claim: Approach A stores `uint64_t snapshot_body_bytes` and `uint64_t removal_body_bytes` on `RefTableState`; the counters exclude header/meta/trailer framing and the removal transaction's terminal `remove_namespace` operation.

topic: The admits() rewrite uses exact framing-size helpers plus
canonical_claim: The `admits()` rewrite uses exact framing-size helpers plus the running body counters rather than hand-written delta arithmetic, while preserving the existing `admits` signature and boolean decisions.

topic: hasAnyRefWithPrefix is intended as an early-exit existence probe
canonical_claim: `hasAnyRefWithPrefix` is intended as an early-exit existence probe that preserves the recovery and stale-precommit maintenance preamble without materializing the full ref map returned by `listRefs`.

topic: The RefTableState optimization work requires a closed class
canonical_claim: The `RefTableState` optimization work requires a closed class whose invariants hold by construction and benchmarks each hot operation before selecting an internal representation by measured performance and code elegance.

topic: The benchmark suite distinguishes BM_AdmitsAddPrecommit, which exercises the
canonical_claim: The benchmark suite distinguishes `BM_AdmitsAddPrecommit`, which exercises the production `manifestAlreadyOwned` scan, from `BM_Admits`, whose promote shape is O(1) and does not exercise that scan.

topic: Experiment E2 represents manifest ownership with a copy-on-write
canonical_claim: Experiment E2 represents manifest ownership with a copy-on-write membership index so uniqueness checks become O(log N) or O(1) without making scratch copies O(N).

topic: Experiment E4 evaluates an immutable shared sorted-vector base
canonical_claim: Experiment E4 evaluates an immutable shared sorted-vector base with an overlay for `RefCowMap`, preserving its ordered-iteration API while reducing pointer-chasing in merged iteration, snapshot encoding, and materialization.

canonical_claim: The pre-release CAS policy permits removing `RefOp::payload` and renaming `SetPayload` to `SetPublishedAt` with wire word `set_payload` to `set_published_at` because every existing pool is recreated before release and no old-field decoder tolerance is required.
